snippets.title: Type-checking JVM stacks across branches
snippets.caption: Part of a JVM bytecode generator built for MSU's compilers course: on every jump, the builder either seeds the target block with the current operand-stack types or checks they match what's already expected there.
snippets.html: if (instruction instanceof Instruction.Branch br) { var block = labeledBlocks.get(br.target()); if (block == null) { assert incoming.label != br.target(); block = new BasicBlock(br.target()); block.entryStack.addAll(newStack); block.tailStack.addAll(newStack); blocks.add(block); labeledBlocks.put(br.target(), block); } else { checkStacks(block.entryStack, newStack, instruction.source()); } incoming.tailStack = newStack; if (br.opcode() == Opcodes.GOTO) { incoming.terminated = true; incoming = null; return; } }

snippets.title: Opaque handles for a C API
snippets.caption: Part of Styx's C bindings: one macro line per type generates a C-visible marker struct `Foo_t` and a `#[repr(transparent)]` handle around a typed opaque pointer, so C code holds safe, typed handles to Rust objects.
snippets.html: macro_rules! opaque_pointer { ( $(#[doc $($doc:tt)+])* pub struct $n:ident($t:ty) ) => { ::paste::paste! { $(#[doc $($doc)+])* #[repr(C)] #[allow(non_camel_case_types)] pub struct [< $n _t >]; impl $crate::data::OpaquePointerType for [< $n _t >] { type To = $t; } #[allow(non_camel_case_types)] #[repr(transparent)] pub struct $n($crate::data::OpaquePointer<[< $n _t >]>);

snippets.title: Operators inferred from the shape of a type
snippets.caption: The derive macro reads each enum variant's fields and decides whether it is a binary, prefix or postfix operator, so a precedence-climbing parser is generated from type definitions alone.
snippets.html: let kind = match ops.as_slice() { [ExprOp::Recurse, ExprOp::Parse(_), ExprOp::Recurse] => StepKind::Binary, [ExprOp::Parse(_), ExprOp::Recurse] => StepKind::Prefix, [ExprOp::Recurse, ExprOp::Parse(_)] => StepKind::Postfix, [] => unreachable!("empty variant"), _ => StepKind::Simple, };

snippets.title: Brace-balanced f-string expressions
snippets.caption: Inside an f-string, the tokenizer tracks nested `{`/`}` depth to cut out exactly one embedded expression, which is then handed to the full Notch parser.
snippets.html: int open = 1; while (true) { if (t.atEnd()) { final var diag = new Diagnostic(); diag.highlight(start); diag.note("unterminated '{' in f-string here"); throw new TokenizeException(diag); } var token = t.nextToken(); if (token.type.equals("}")) { open -= 1; if (open == 0) break; } if (token.type.equals("{")) open += 1; tokens.add(token); }

snippets.title: Parsing calls with error recovery
snippets.caption: From Sea, a simplified C for teaching systems programming: the call-argument loop doesn't stop at the first bad token, it turns it into an error node and keeps parsing.
snippets.html: while (sea_parser_more(parser) && !sea_parser_match(parser, ")")) { start = sea_parser_peek(parser); arg = sea_parse_expr(parser); if (!arg) { arg = malloc(sizeof(sea_expr)); arg->type = SEA_EXPR_ERROR; arg->item = sea_token_clone(sea_parser_adv(parser)); arg->error = sea_make_error("Expected expression as argument", start, arg->item); } vec_sea_expr_append(call->args, arg); if (!sea_parser_match(parser, ",")) { break; } else { sea_parser_adv(parser); } }

snippets.title: Racing tasks to a graceful shutdown
snippets.caption: From a grading server for MSU's security course: the first task to finish trips a shared shutdown flag, and the rest get 10 seconds to drain before the process exits.
snippets.html: let mut fu = FuturesUnordered::from_iter(tasks); let _ = fu.next().await; flag.set(); eprintln!("shutting down!"); let end = async { while fu.next().await.is_some() { continue; } }; tokio::select! { _ = end => {} _ = tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(10)) => {} }

snippets.title: Any closure is a parser primitive
snippets.caption: A blanket impl over `FnOnce(char) -> bool` means `parser.take(char::is_whitespace)` works right alongside the `char`, `&str` and `[char; N]` impls.
snippets.html: impl<T: FnOnce(char) -> bool> ParsePrimitive for T { fn peek(self, parser: &Parser) -> bool { parser.source[parser.location.index..] .chars() .next() .is_some_and(self) } fn take(self, parser: &mut Parser) -> bool { parser.source[parser.location.index..] .chars() .next() .filter(|c| self(*c)) .inspect(|c| parser.location.advance(*c)) .is_some() } fn len(&self) -> usize { 1 } }

snippets.title: Python hooks from an X-macro
snippets.caption: Styx's Python bindings list every emulator hook once in an X-macro; `define_hooks!` turns each entry into a pyo3 class that wraps a Python callback and bridges it to the Rust hook trait.
snippets.html: macro_rules! define_hooks { ( $( $name:ident( $($an:ident: $at:ty: $att:ty),* $(,)? ) $(-> $rt:ty: $rtt:ty)? $({ $($pn:ident: $pt:ty),* $(,)? })? ;)* ) => { $( ::paste::paste! { #[gen_stub_pyclass] #[pyclass(module = "cpu.hooks")] #[derive(Clone)] pub struct [< $name Hook >] { $( $($pn: $pt,)*)? callback: std::sync::Arc<PyObject>, }

snippets.title: Pinch-zoom that stops softly
snippets.caption: When a pinch on the periodic table goes past the zoom limits, the zoom-centring offset is scaled back by the same fraction, so it stops at the limit instead of jumping.
snippets.html: double newScale = provider.scale * scaleDelta; if (newScale < minScale) { double t = (provider.scale - minScale) / (provider.scale - newScale); scaleOffset = Offset.lerp(Offset.zero, scaleOffset, t); newScale = minScale; } if (newScale > maxScale) { double t = (maxScale - provider.scale) / (newScale - provider.scale); scaleOffset = Offset.lerp(Offset.zero, scaleOffset, t); newScale = maxScale; }

snippets.title: A tiny DSL for running commands
snippets.caption: `cmd!` takes an optional `in dir;`, variadic args and an inline configuration hook, and fails at compile time with a clear message when called empty.
snippets.html: macro_rules! cmd { ( $(in $path:expr;)? $cmd:expr $(, $($e:expr),*)? $(,)? $(; fn $name:ident => $body:expr)? ) => {{ let mut command = Command::new(AsRef::<OsStr>::as_ref(&$cmd)); $(command.current_dir($path);)? $(command.args(&[ $(AsRef::<OsStr>::as_ref(&$e)),* ]);)? $({ let $name = &mut command; $body; })? eprintln!("CMD: {:?}", command); cmd(&mut command) }}; () => { compile_error!("cmd! macro requires at least a command name") } }

snippets.title: Catching edited autograder releases
snippets.caption: Autograder results are published as GitHub releases. If a student edits one, this action snapshots the edit event as an artifact and opens an issue for the instructor.
snippets.html: steps: - run: | cp $GITHUB_EVENT_PATH release - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4 id: upload-release-diff with: name: Release Diff path: release if-no-files-found: error retention-days: 90 overwrite: false - uses: actions/checkout@v3 - uses: JasonEtco/create-an-issue@v2 env: GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} ARTIFACT_URL: ${{ steps.upload-release-diff.outputs.artifact-url }} with: filename: .github/ANTICHEAT_TEMPLATE.md

snippets.title: One fold for every precedence level
snippets.caption: A generic left fold turns a flat list like `a * b / c` into a left-associative syntax tree, so each binary-operator level of the parser is a one-liner.
snippets.html: public E fold(TriFunction<E, E, Token, E> func) { if (items.isEmpty()) return last; var iterator = items.iterator(); Pair<E, Token> last = iterator.next(); E acc = last.left(); while (iterator.hasNext()) { var next = iterator.next(); acc = func.apply(acc, next.left(), last.right()); last = next; } return func.apply(acc, this.last, last.right()); }

snippets.title: Sudoku as wave function collapse
snippets.caption: Sudoku expressed as rules for a generic wave-function-collapse solver: a cell may hold whatever its row, column and 3×3 block leave over.
snippets.html: let row = map.row(); let col = map.col(); let (x, y) = map.pos(); let block = map.section_at(3, 3, *x, *y); let row_states = states(row.row_iter()); let col_states = states(col.row_iter()); let block_states = states(block.row_iter()); let mut possible = SudokuNum::full_set(); for states in [row_states, col_states, block_states] { for state in states { possible.remove(state); } } possible

snippets.title: An if / else-if chain from a quote! repetition
snippets.caption: Using `else` as the repetition separator turns a list of variant parsers into one `if let … else if let … else` chain, with a type-named error as the fallback.
snippets.html: fn impl_parse_variants(&self) -> Result<TokenStream, Error> { let variants = self .item .variants .iter() .map(|variant| self.impl_parse_variant(variant)) .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?; Ok(quote! { return #(#variants)else* else { Err(input.mismatch(format!("expected {}", std::any::type_name::<Self>()))) }; }) }

snippets.title: Route matching with captured variables
snippets.caption: The core of a Dart router: matches a path segment by segment, checks optional per-segment regex constraints, and captures path variables as it goes.
snippets.html: for (int i = 0; i < uri.segments.length; i++) { final PathSegment segment = uri.segments[i]; final String intent = raw.pathSegments[i]; if (segment.isVariable) { if (segment.matcher != null) { if (!segment.matcher!.hasMatch(intent)) { isMatch = false; break; } } variables[segment.name] = intent; continue; } if (segment.name != intent) { isMatch = false; break; } }
